verses.7:53: ⟦And each one went to his own house.⟧
verses.8:1: ⟦But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.⟧
verses.8:2: ⟦And at dawn He came again into the temple, and all the people were coming; and having sat down, He began teaching them.⟧
verses.8:3: ⟦Now the scribes and the Pharisees bring to Him a woman caught in adultery; and having set her in the middle,⟧
verses.8:4: ⟦they say to Him, testing Him, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery.⟧
verses.8:5: ⟦Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such women; what then do You say?"⟧
verses.8:6: ⟦Now they were saying this to test Him, so that they might have grounds to accuse Him. But Jesus, bending down, was writing with His finger on the ground, acting as though He did not notice.⟧
verses.8:7: ⟦Yet as they persisted in questioning Him, He straightened up and said to them, "Let the one among you who is without sin throw the stone at her first."⟧
verses.8:8: ⟦And bending down again, He was writing on the ground.⟧
verses.8:9: ⟦Now they, when they heard it and were convicted by their conscience, began going out one by one, starting from the elders; and Jesus alone was left, and the woman who was in the middle.⟧
verses.8:10: ⟦Then Jesus straightened up and, seeing no one except the woman, said to her, "Where are those accusers of yours? Did no one condemn you?"⟧
verses.8:11: ⟦And she said, "No one, Lord." And Jesus said, "Neither do I judge you; go, and sin no more."⟧

notes.7:53: Double brackets ⟦ ⟧ are preserved around 7:53–8:11 exactly as in the Saints Greek Critical Text, marking the pericope of the adulterous woman, which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:6: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes the participial phrase μὴ προσποιούμενος ("not taking notice / acting as though He did not notice"), which is translated here.
notes.8:7: τὸν λίθον carries the definite article ("the stone"), referring to the first stone in a stoning execution, and πρῶτον is adverbial ("first").
notes.8:9: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς συνειδήσεως ἐλεγχόμενοι ("and being convicted by their conscience"), which appears in the Byzantine textual tradition.
notes.8:11: While 8:10 uses κατέκρινεν ("condemn"), the Saints Greek Critical Text here reads the simple verb κρίνω ("judge"), preserved distinctly as "judge."
